slides.headline: Houthis battle for control of front-line Taiz
slides.body: Rare access from inside Yemen’s conflict zone shows pro-government soldiers at the front line as Houthi forces fight around Taiz.

slides.headline: That follows a war that began in late 2014
slides.body: The civil war began after Houthi forces took Sanaa, and the UN says more than 150,000 people have been killed in the conflict.

slides.headline: The reason: Houthis took Sanaa in 2014
slides.body: Houthi forces took Yemen’s capital in September 2014, and rival authorities now claim to govern the country.

slides.headline: And about 24 million Yemenis have needed aid
slides.body: Yemen has an estimated 34.7 million people, and the UN reported in 2019 that about 24 million needed humanitarian aid.

slides.headline: Which puts the Red Sea in the conflict
slides.body: Yemen borders the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, and the conflict now extends into Red Sea security concerns.

slides.body: Yemen government forces have widened attacks against the Houthis as fighting intensifies around Taiz’s western approaches.
